outcome: Help rights teams understand ownership, territory, window, platform, talent and royalty obligations before use and payment.
overview: Rights and obligations live in contracts and spreadsheets disconnected from the assets they cover and the usage they govern, so windows are missed, royalties are overpaid or underpaid, and disputes are settled from memory. This solution extracts terms from licence agreements, builds a rights graph linking title, territory, window, platform and talent obligations to the assets themselves, then reconciles that graph against actual distribution and usage. Every recommendation cites the clause it came from and carries a confidence indicator, and legal and finance approve before anything is published or paid. An 8–14 week pilot on one contract set targets faster clearance and better obligation matching.

benefits.text: Reduce contract and clearance processing time by a target 30% on the pilot contract set
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Target from the source catalogue, to validate against the rights team’s own processing baseline during the pilot — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Improve matching between contractual obligations and actual usage, exposing missed revenue and overpayment
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on the completeness of distribution and usage records; any recovered or avoided value is confirmed by finance, never claimed by the system

benefits.text: Trace every rights and payment recommendation back to the contract clause and version that produced it
benefits.source: Architecture design — extraction stores clause citations and contract versions with each derived obligation
benefits.limits: Traceability shows which clause was relied on, not that the interpretation is correct; the signed contract remains authoritative and system output is not legal advice

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); contracts, rights records, usage data and payment calculations remain in the customer tenancy in the reference designs

notFor.situation: Contracts exist only as unsearchable scans or paper with no digitisation plan
notFor.why: Extraction operates on readable documents; the pilot cannot build a rights graph from material it cannot open

notFor.situation: Automated royalty payment without legal and finance approval is the goal
notFor.why: Payment and distribution decisions carry contractual liability and stay with legal and finance by design; the system prepares, it does not authorise

notFor.situation: Ownership itself is disputed across the catalogue in scope
notFor.why: A rights graph records what contracts say; where the parties disagree about ownership the answer is a legal process, not a data platform

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns contract interpretation, legal approval and every payment decision · Duration: 8–14 week PoV; further 18–30 weeks to enterprise rollout
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, document-extraction engineer, data engineer; customer rights owner, legal counsel, royalty and finance lead, security approver · Support model: Business-hours or 24×7 option; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Discovery and baseline agreement
2) Contract repository preparation and rights-taxonomy design
3) Extraction tuning against a lawyer-approved benchmark
4) Rights graph, workbench and reconciliation build
5) Legal and finance UAT with controlled rollout
6) Stabilisation and handover
deliverables: Extraction accuracy meets the agreed threshold on the lawyer-approved benchmark
Rights, usage and payment reconciliation ties to the source systems
Ambiguous and low-confidence clauses route to legal rather than resolving automatically
Permissions, confidentiality and security review passed on contract data
Legal and finance UAT complete with sign-off recorded
effort: 8–14 week PoV; further 18–30 weeks to enterprise rollout
languages: Arabic and English contract extraction with bilingual clause review; delivery in English with Arabic legal-review support
